messages.author: 4c67c305cf9c2e1b
messages.subject: "occuMulti" doubts about occupancy results
parts:
Hello, I've been using the "occuMulti" function to fit the Rota et al (2016) models for two species, A and B... When I do; predict(model_x, type="state"), I get psi[11], psi[10], psi[01] and psi[00], when I do; predict(model_x, 'state', species=c('A','B')) the results match the ones in psi[11], but when I do; predict(model_x, type = "state", species = "A", cond = "-B"), the results do not match the ones in psi[10] and as far as I know they should mean the same thing... would anyone know what causes this difference?

Obs. predict(model_x, type = "state", species = "B", cond = "-A") results also don't match what is in psi[01].

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: "occuMulti" doubts about occupancy results
parts:
When you put two species in to the 'species' argument you are getting the total probability of states in which the two species occur. So in a two species system this is indeed just psi[11] since that is the only possible state in which both occur.

When you calculate occupancy of species A conditional on the absence of species B, you are changing the denominator of the calculation. It is the sum of probability of states where species A is present and species B is absent, divided by the the sum of the probability of states where species B is absent. Thus, in your example the result from predict is calculated as psi[10] / (psi[10] + psi[00]). See eqn 4 in Rota et al. 2016.

Ken

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: "occuMulti" doubts about occupancy results
parts:
* Say you have psi[11] = 0.3, psi[10] = 0.1, psi[01] = 0.4, and psi[00] = 0.2 (total = 1)
* Also assume there are 100 sites, so that 30 sites (0.3*100) contain both species A and B, 10 sites contain only species A, 40 sites contain only species B, and 20 sites contain neither species.

psi[10] represents the probability that a given site you pick at random out of the full set of sites will contain, specifically, species A but not species B: 10 sites / 100 total sites  = 0.1

When you are calculating the probability of occupancy of species A *conditional* on the absence of species B, you are asking: if I pick a site at random from *only sites that do not contain species B*, what is the probability that this site will contain species A? To answer that question, you need to know how many sites contained A but not B (i.e., 10), and also how many total sites did not have species B: 10 sites had A but not B, and  20 sites had neither A nor B, for a total of 30 sites with no B.  Thus out of the 30 possible sites that did not contain B, 10 of those sites contained A: 10/30 = 0.33 is the conditional probability

or, following eqn 4 and using the probabilities instead:

psi[10] / (psi[10] psi[00]) = 0.1 / (0.1 + 0.2) = 0.33

Does that help?
